paper_title: PhysSkin++: Real-Time and Generalizable Physics-Based Animation via Self-Supervised Neural Skinning

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Generalizing real-time physics-based animation across diverse 3D shapes and spatial discretizations remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce PhysSkin++, a physics-informed framework that learns continuous neural skinning fields from static geometries to construct compact deformation subspaces. Specifically, we propose a Neural Skinning Fields Autoencoder that predicts shape-dependent deformation subspaces without per-object network training. To learn these subspaces without simulation trajectories, we develop a Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Learning strategy that combines skinning-field normalization with conflict-aware gradient correction, stabilizing joint optimization under physical and orthogonality constraints. The learned representation supports efficient reduced dynamics with user control and contact interactions, together with direct animation binding to meshes, point clouds, and 3D Gaussians. For prescribed rig animation, we further introduce a self-supervised complementarity objective to learn complementary elastic responses without enforcing complementarity constraints at runtime. Experiments demonstrate cross-shape generalization of the learned skinning fields, real-time reduced simulation, and applications to controllable, collision-aware, and rig-complementary animation.

sections.content: PhysSkin++: Real-Time and Generalizable Physics-Based Animation via Self-Supervised Neural Skinning Yuanhang Lei, Baofei Liu, Xingxuan Li, Tao Cheng, Zixuan Wang, Boming Zhao, Yujun Shen, Siyuan Huang, Ruizhen Hu, Peter Yichen Chen, Hujun Bao, and Zhaopeng Cui 1 AbstractGeneralizing real-time physics-based animation across diverse 3D shapes and spatial discretizations remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce PhysSkin++, physicsinformed framework that learns continuous neural skinning fields from static geometries to construct compact deformation subspaces. Specifically, we propose Neural Skinning Fields Autoencoder that predicts shape-dependent deformation subspaces without per-object network training. To learn these subspaces without simulation trajectories, we develop Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Learning strategy that combines skinning-field normalization with conflict-aware gradient correction, stabilizing joint optimization under physical and orthogonality constraints. The learned representation supports efficient reduced dynamics with user control and contact interactions, together with direct animation binding to meshes, point clouds, and 3D Gaussians. For prescribed rig animation, we further introduce self-supervised complementarity objective to learn complementary elastic responses without enforcing complementarity constraints at runtime. Experiments demonstrate cross-shape generalization of the learned skinning fields, real-time reduced simulation, and applications to controllable, collision-aware, and rig-complementary animation. Project page: https://zju3dv.github.io/PhysSkin plus/. Index TermsPhysics-based animation, geometric deep learning, reduced-order modeling, self-supervised learning. I. INTRODUCTION Real-time physics-based animation is long-standing goal in computer vision and graphics, underpinning applications in VR/AR authoring, character animation, and interactive digital content creation. To support such applications, an animation system must provide compact yet expressive motion representation that captures physically plausible deformations, accommodates user control and interactions, and remains computationally efficient for real-time animation. Subspace physics-based animation [2], [10] addresses this by learning low-dimensional motion subspace for efficient computation, and then lifting the result back to the full space using subspace mapping. However, classical methods [2], [51] optimize single linear subspace mapping matrix tied to particular mesh topology and resolution, which prevents generalization across different spatial discretizations. Recently, Corresponding author. Yuanhang Lei, Baofei Liu, Xingxuan Li, Tao Cheng, Zixuan Wang, Boming Zhao, Hujun Bao, and Zhaopeng Cui are with the State Key Laboratory of CAD&CG, Zhejiang University. Yujun Shen is with Ant Group, Hangzhou 310000, China. Siyuan Huang is with the Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence (BIGAI). Ruizhen Hu is with Shenzhen University. Peter Yichen Chen is with the University of British Columbia. neural methods [10], [49] have emerged as promising alternatives by using neural networks to learn subspace mappings that naturally handle arbitrary spatial discretizations. These approaches, however, must still train separate network per object and fail to generalize to different 3D shapes. In parallel, recent transformer-based approaches learn physical dynamics directly from simulation trajectories across diverse objects and physical systems [15], [58]. Although this data-driven route enables generalizable neural simulation, it requires extensive trajectory supervision and does not explicitly construct lowdimensional deformation subspace for reduced-order animation. These limitations motivate central question: How can we learn physics-consistent deformation subspace mapping that generalizes across diverse 3D shapes and discretizations directly from static geometries, without relying on supervised training data? In this work, we introduce PhysSkin++  (Fig. 1)  , generalizable physics-informed framework for real-time physicsbased animation across diverse 3D shapes and discretizations. In the spirit of Linear Blend Skinning (LBS) [43], we use continuous skinning fields to define deformation subspace mapping, with handle transformations serving as the reduced coordinates for full-space 3D object deformation. To construct this representation directly from static geometries, we introduce Neural Skinning Fields Autoencoder. Specifically, PhysSkin++ employs transformer-based point cloud encoder to extract latent shape features from surface samples, while crossattention decoder predicts continuous neural skinning fields at arbitrary spatial locations. PhysSkin++ requires no simulation trajectories, skinning annotations, or category-specific priors. This mesh-free, discretization-agnostic representation generalizes across object categories, topologies, and resolutions. Learning such deformation subspace mapping purely from geometry is highly non-trivial. physically meaningful subspace must exhibit low potential energy, reflecting deformation modes compatible with physically plausible behavior; spatial smoothness, ensuring coherent deformations; and orthogonality, promoting independence among the deformation modes. We therefore formulate self-supervised objective consisting of potential-energy, smoothness, and orthogonality terms. However, jointly optimizing these terms often leads to conflicts in gradient magnitude and direction, making naive joint optimization unstable. To overcome this optimization challenge, we introduce Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Learning (PISSL) strategy. First, we apply on-the-fly skinningfield normalization, which regulates the scale of the learned skinning weights and prevents numerical drift during training. Fig. 1. PhysSkin++ is generalizable physics-informed neural skinning framework for object animation. The framework is learned directly from static 3D geometries via physics-informed self-supervision without any annotated data. Once trained, PhysSkin++ can be applied in feed-forward manner to perform neural skinning for diverse 3D shapes and discretizations, enabling real-time physics-based animation. It further supports interactive control, collision-aware multi-object interaction, and rig-complementary animation. Second, we incorporate conflict-aware gradient correction mechanism [37] to resolve destructive interference among gradients of the loss terms, enabling balanced optimization and stable convergence. Together, these mechanisms enable PhysSkin++ to learn physically consistent deformation subspace mapping directly from static geometries, with spatially smooth and approximately orthogonal skinning fields. At runtime, we advance the reduced coordinates through implicit reduced dynamics and map them to full-space deformations through the learned skinning-based subspace mapping. To support controllable and collision-aware animation, we incorporate Dirichlet boundary conditions, interactive control, environmental interaction, and multi-object contact into this formulation. Prescribed boundary displacements are enforced through boundary-compatible deformation map, while external forces and contact interactions are incorporated through their corresponding energy terms. This formulation supports both rigiddeformable and deformabledeformable interactions within the learned deformation subspaces. Moreover, the continuous deformation map can be directly bound to different spatial discretizations, including 3D Gaussian representations [28], enabling physics-based animation of diverse object representations within the same reduced dynamics framework. Beyond purely physics-driven animation, PhysSkin++ also supports rig-complementary animation when an artist-authored LBS rig is available. Artist-authored rigs provide intuitive lowdimensional control, but their kinematic deformations alone cannot reproduce physical elastic responses, while increasing the complexity of rig places greater burden on animation authoring. Complementary dynamics [6], [65] addresses this tension by augmenting prescribed rig animation with complementary physical deformations. Following this principle, PhysSkin++ treats the user-authored rig-based animation as the primary animation and learns neural skinning fields for complementary elastic response. We augment the self-supervised objective with rig-space complementarity term defined by the rig Jacobian, encouraging the learned deformation subspace to be complementary to the prescribed rig animation space. At runtime, the resulting reduced dynamics enriches the prescribed animation with physics-based complementary displacement without enforcing the rig-space complementarity constraint at every step. Both animation settings share the continuous skinning representation and reduced dynamics framework. Experiments on various datasets evaluate the learned skinning fields and demonstrate real-time physics-based animation across diverse shapes, controls, interactions, and spatial discretizations. Our contributions are: We present PhysSkin++, generalizable physics-informed framework for real-time physics-based animation across diverse 3D shapes and discretizations by learning neural skinning fields directly from static geometries. Its Neural Skinning Fields Autoencoder employs transformer-based shape encoder and cross-attention decoder to predict continuous skinning fields. We develop Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Learning (PISSL) strategy that incorporates on-the-fly skinningfield normalization and conflict-aware gradient correction, enabling stable joint optimization of multiple selfsupervised loss terms. We develop controllable and collision-aware reduced dynamics formulation that supports Dirichlet boundary conditions, interactive control, environmental interaction, and multi-object contact, together with discretizationagnostic binding of the continuous deformation map to meshes, point clouds, and 3D Gaussian representations. We support rig-complementary animation by extending the self-supervised objective with rig-space complementarity term defined by the rig Jacobian. This enables physics-based complementary elastic responses under interactive rig control and user-authored animation se2 quences without enforcing the rig-space complementarity constraint at runtime. preliminary version of this work has been published as PhysSkin [30]. The present article extends the conference version in four aspects. First, we develop reduced dynamics formulation for controllable and collision-aware animation, supporting prescribed boundary displacements, interactive control, environmental interaction, and multi-object contact. Second, we provide discretization-agnostic binding formulation for 3D Gaussian representations, updating both Gaussian centers and anisotropic covariances through local affine transformations determined by the learned skinning fields and current reduced coordinates. Third, we extend the deformation representation with prescribed rig displacement and the self-supervised objective with rig-space complementarity term. These extensions support complementary elastic deformation for prescribed rig animations without enforcing the complementarity constraint at runtime. Finally, we expand the experimental evaluation to cover controllable and collision-aware animation, 3D Gaussian animation, and self-supervised rig-complementarity learning, including rig-complementary animation under interactive rig control and user-authored animation sequences. II. RELATED WORK Neural Physics-Based Animation. Subspace physics-based animation [2], [10], [57] is an effective method for accelerating animation computations. Its core idea is to learn lowdimensional motion subspace for efficient computation, and then lift the result back to the full space using subspace mapping. Recently, fully neural approaches have been proposed to directly learn subspace mapping by neural networks. Datadriven methods [9], [10], [17], [50], [68] represented by CROM [10] learn the mapping for single object by fitting neural networks to motion sequences from physical simulators, but they have limited generalization ability to unseen motion patterns. In parallel, recent transformer-based approaches learn physical dynamics directly from simulation trajectories across rigid, deformable, and particle-based systems [12], [15], [19], [58]. Data-free methods [8], [41], [44], [49], [59] learn low-energy subspace mapping by physics-informed learning without requiring motion sequences, but pure neural network approaches often struggle to converge to high-quality subspace representations. Recently, Simplicits [44] learns neural skinning weight functions as physics-informed subspace mapping by minimizing quadratic energy subject to orthogonality constraints, which stabilizes training compared to purely neural models but limits generalization due to its per-object network design. Our method overcomes these limitations with neural skinning fields autoencoder that outputs skinning weights generalizing across diverse 3D shapes, enabling real-time subspace physics-based animation. Our physics-informed neural subspace formulation retains explicit reduced-order dynamics and complements approaches that learn dynamics directly from simulation trajectories. Neural Rigging and Skinning Representations. Another classical reduced deformation representation is skeletal riggingbased animation [5], [16], [39]. Recently, based on 3D shape 3 VAEs [64], [67], many works [14], [20], [36], [52], [53], [62], [66] have performed supervised learning from expert-annotated 3D object rigging and skinning datasets to infer objects joints, bones, and skinning weights through feed-forward network. However, some methods are limited to specific categories of 3D shapes such as characters [20], [62] or animals [55], [60], as they incorporate category-specific priors [39], [69] such as predefined skeletal structures or semantic constraints, making it difficult to generalize to other object categories. Works represented by Anymate [14] learn from annotated 3D object rigging and skinning datasets and design category-agnostic network architectures, thereby enabling the ability to generalize across diverse object categories and demonstrating stronger generalization capabilities. However, these methods heavily rely on expert-annotated data [14], [34], [35], [40], [60], which are costly and difficult to scale. In contrast, our work employs self-supervised learning to train neural skinning fields directly from static 3D geometries without any annotated data. A. Framework Overview and Problem Formulation III. METHOD PhysSkin++ is generalizable physics-informed framework for real-time physics-based animation across diverse 3D shapes and discretizations. As illustrated in Fig. 2, our neural skinning fields autoencoder predicts continuous skinning fields from static geometry to define deformation subspace mapping. The autoencoder is trained through Physics-Informed SelfSupervised Learning (PISSL) under physical and numerical constraints. At runtime, we advance reduced coordinates to animate objects with boundary conditions, interactive control, and contact. Beyond purely physics-driven animation, PhysSkin++ also supports rig-complementary animation by learning complementary deformation subspaces for prescribed rigs. Moreover, the continuous deformation map supports binding to mesh vertices, sampled points, and 3D Gaussians. Classical full-space physics-based animation methods [27], [31], [38], [51], [61], [63] typically use explicit or implicit time integrators to update the objects motion state. Explicit time integrators are often constrained by stability conditions [33], while implicit time integrators require solving large nonlinear optimization problem in the high-dimensional full space. PhysSkin++ instead represents the deformation using continuous neural skinning fields and advances only the corresponding reduced-order subspace coordinates through implicit time integration. This lower-dimensional optimization reduces computational cost [6], enabling real-time physicsbased animation. Continuous Skinning-Based Deformation Representation. III-E. B. Neural Skinning Fields Autoencoder We train neural skinning fields autoencoder to predict spatially continuous skinning weights across diverse 3D shapes and discretizations. The resulting mesh-free representation supports the skinning-based real-time animation described in Sec. III-D. Unlike existing neural subspace methods [10], [44] that train separate neural network for each object, our single feedforward network generalizes across diverse objects, improving scalability and practicality. Neural 3D Shape Encoding. We use the transformer-based point cloud encoder Michelangelo [67] to extract highly compressed latent set Fs RM for given 3D shape via cross-attention block and several self-attention blocks: Fs = SelfAttn(1:L)(CrossAttn(Qs, γ(P))), (2) where Qs RM is set of learnable shape latent tokens, RN 6 is the sampled surface point cloud with points, each point consisting of 3D coordinates and normals, γ() is point-wise positional encoding, SelfAttn(1:L)() indicates stack of self-attention layers that iteratively improve the shape latent representation, is the number of latents, and is the dimension of each latent. In practice, the shape encoder is pretrained on the ShapeNet dataset [7] via signed distance field (SDF) reconstruction task [47] to learn generalizable geometric priors. We then freeze the encoder parameters during training to enhance efficiency. Neural Skinning Fields Decoding. To obtain spatially continuous skinning fields, we decode the shape latent set Fs obtained from Eq. (2) into spatially varying skinning weights. (3) Next, for any spatial query point X, we use another crossattention block to extract point-wise skinning feature Fp Rd from the skinning handle latent set Fh: Fp = CrossAttn(γ(X), Fh). To promote orthogonality among different skinning modes, we apply an Orthogonalization by Newtons Iteration (ONI) module [26] at the final layer of the MLP, and we adopt ELU as the activation function in the MLP, which allows learning flexible and expressive skinning-based deformation subspaces without enforcing non-negativity on the learned skinning modes. The continuous fields can be queried throughout the object, while cubature points specify locations for physics-informed training and numerical integration. Cubature Points Sampling. In the classical Finite Element Method (FEM) [51], the objects volume is typically discretized into tetrahedral mesh [23] to facilitate numerical solutions of physical equations. Unlike triangle surface meshes commonly used for rendering, which only contain surface points, tetrahedral meshes include interior volumetric elements that better capture the objects spatial structure. To train the neural skinning fields autoencoder, we sample cubature points both on the objects surface and inside its volume, with each cubature point serving as spatial query point for computing the potential energy Epot during subspace learning and skinningbased real-time animation. This sampling captures volumetric deformation behavior that surface-only sampling cannot, in contrast to popular 3D Shape VAEs [64] that only sample surface points. To sample interior cubature points, we first convert the objects surface mesh into watertight mesh [24], [25], then uniformly sample points in the voxelized spatial grid using ray tracing [45], and classify points as being outside the object if the ray intersects the surface mesh and the dot product with the normal is negative. For surface cubature points, we employ Sharp Edge Sampling (SES) [11] to better capture geometric details. C. Rig-Complementary Animation Beyond purely physics-driven animation, PhysSkin++ also supports rig-complementary animation when an artist-authored LBS rig is available. The prescribed rig deformation serves as the primary animation, while complementary elastic deformation is parameterized by reduced coordinates through the learned neural skinning fields. We first describe the rig-based deformation and then introduce the rig-space complementarity objective used during self-supervised learning. Rig-Based Deformation Representation. Consider skeletal rig with nb bones, pose parameters p, and rest pose p0. Let Gb(p) SE(3) be the global transformation of bone b, obtained by composing its local transformations along the kinematic hierarchy. We denote by Ab(p) R34 the affine transform induced by the relative bone motion Gb(p)Gb(p0)1. In this paper, we present PhysSkin++, generalizable physics-informed framework for real-time physics-based animation across diverse 3D shapes and discretizations. neural skinning fields autoencoder learns continuous skinning fields directly from static geometries to define skinning-based subspace mapping. Our Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Learning (PISSL) strategy promotes physically plausible deformations through self-supervised objective and stabilizes joint optimization through on-the-fly skinning-field normalization and conflict-aware gradient correction. At runtime, reduced dynamics formulation advances the reduced coordinates and 14 supports Dirichlet boundary conditions, interactive control, environmental interaction, and both rigiddeformable and deformabledeformable contact. Beyond purely physics-driven animation, we extend the deformation representation with prescribed rig displacement and the self-supervised objective with rig-space complementarity term, enabling complementary elastic responses for prescribed rig animations without enforcing the complementarity constraint at runtime. The continuous deformation map also enables discretization-agnostic binding to meshes, point clouds, and 3D Gaussian representations. Experiments demonstrate that PhysSkin++ achieves outstanding performance on generalizable neural skinning while enabling real-time physics-based animation. As limitation, our current formulation does not incorporate semantic priors for modeling complex geometries.
